'''Warren Palmer Waters''' (8 September 1922 – 17 July 2000) was an American [[physicist]], electrical engineer, and [[semiconductor]] pioneer. He filed several device and process patents in the field of [[Solid-state electronics|solid state engineering]] and was the manager of the solid state research center for the [[Hughes Aircraft Company]]. Walter's innovative circuit designs led to the success of [[NASA]]'s [[Surveyor program]].

== Education and military service ==
Waters was born in Sanger, California on 8 September 1922.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Warren P. Waters |url=https://www.atomicheritage.org/profile/warren-p-waters |access-date=2020-08-14 |website=Atomic Heritage Foundation |language=en}}</ref> He graduated with honors from Sanger High School, winning the [[Bausch & Lomb#20th century|Bausch+Lomb Honorary Science Award]] for chemistry.<ref name=":1" />

Waters joined the [[United States Army|U.S. Army]] in 1942 and trained to be a pilot during World War II. He was later deployed to the 386th Infantry division in northern France.<ref name=":0" /> He lost a leg in combat on 12 April 1945, and received a Purple Heart<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Purple Heart Hall of Honor |url=https://www.thepurpleheart.com/roll-of-honor/recipients/?name=Waters,+Warren&conflict=&branch= |access-date=2020-08-14 |website=www.thepurpleheart.com}}</ref><ref name="purple">{{cite web |title=Purple Heart Recipient |url=http://www.thepurpleheart.com/recipient/RecipientDetails.aspx?rid=d85028bb-f28d-4250-a6d0-4dc03c3f46cc&aid=5CA7 |access-date=24 June 2015 |website=The National Purple Heart Hall of Honor |publisher=thepurpleheart.com }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and a Bronze Star for his service.<ref name=":0" />

Waters graduated from [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] in 1949.<ref name="caltech">{{cite news |title=Personals: 1949 |work=Engineering and Science |publisher=[[Caltech]] |issue=pg. 24–26 |url=http://calteches.library.caltech.edu/662/2/Personals.pdf |access-date=24 June 2015}}</ref> He received his master's degree from the [[University of Southern California]] in 1954<ref name="thesis">{{cite journal|last1=Waters|first1=Warren P.|date=June 1954|title=Some Experimental Studies with AC Operated Positive Ion Space Charge Detector|journal=University of Southern California Library, M.S. Thesis}}</ref> and completed coursework there for a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in physics.<ref name=":0" />

== Scientific career ==
[[File:Warren_P._Waters_at_Hughes_Aircraft_1954.jpg|right|thumb|257x257px|Warren P. Waters at Hughes Aircraft, 1954]]
Waters spent his summers between 1947 and 1951 working at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]], helping test new rocket designs.<ref name=":0" />

Waters joined the [[Hughes Aircraft Company]] in 1952<ref name="caltech" /><ref name="hughes">{{cite news |date=3 March 1966 |title=Hughes Tabs NB Research Center Chief |page=157 |publisher=Independent Press-Telegram |agency=[[Hughes Aircraft Company|Hughes News]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/19443390/ |access-date=23 June 2015}}</ref> and was involved in pioneering research on germanium<ref name="gold-bonded">{{cite journal |author1=Sverre T. Eng |author2=Warren P. Waters |date=14 October 1959 |title=A Gold-Bonded Germanium Diode for Parametric Amplification |journal=Proceedings of the National Electronics Conference |volume=XV |pages=15, 83–91}}</ref> and silicon [[Bipolar junction transistor|bipolar transistors]].<ref name="WorldCat">{{cite book |last1=Waters |first1=Warren P. |url=http://www.worldcat.org/identities/np-waters,%20warren%20p/ |title=HIGH FREQUENCY TRANSISTOR STUDY |date=1961 |publisher=WorldCat Idendities |access-date=24 June 2015}}</ref><ref name="SiliconFusionTransistors">{{cite journal|author1=R. A. Gudmundsen|author2=A. L. Wannlund|author3=W. P. Waters|author4=W. V. Wright|date=December 1945|title=Recent Developments in Silicon Fusion Transistors|journal=Tele-Tech & Electronic Industries|pages=76–78, 149–150}}</ref><ref name="SiliconPNP">{{cite journal|author1=Arthur L. Wannlund|author2=Warren P. Waters|date=1957|title=A Silicon PNP Fused-Junction Transistor|journal=IRE 1957 WESCON Convention Record Part 3 "Electron Devices"|publisher=Hughes Semiconductors|pages=3–13}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Warren P. Waters|author2=H. G. Dill|author3=C. H. Fa|title=Molecular Bandpass Amplifiers|journal=AF Report|volume=ASD-TDR-62-21}}</ref> He filed five patents during this period.<ref name="autofluxing">{{cite journal |author1=Warren P Waters |author2=Jon H Myer |date=24 Dec 1957 |title=Alkali metal alloy agents for autofluxing in junction forming |url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US2817609 |location=Hughes Aircraft Co |access-date=24 June 2015}}</ref><ref name="fused-junction">{{cite journal |author1=Warren P Waters |date=8 April 1958 |title=Process for making fused junction semiconductor devices with alkali metalgallium alloy |url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US2829993 |location=Hughes Aircraft Co |access-date=24 June 2015}}</ref>

In 1962, he joined [[Texas Instruments]] to manage its department for [[semiconductor]] research and advanced device development.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=March 6, 1966 |title=Waters back with Hughes |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/719769092 |access-date=2022-11-14 |website=Newspapers.com |publisher=Independent |location=Long Beach, California |language=en}}</ref>

In 1966, Waters returned to Hughes as the manager of its solid state research center in 1966,<ref name="hughes" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name="Man-of-the-hour">{{cite news|date=1966|title=Warren Waters: Man-of-the-hour|publisher=[[Hughes Aircraft Company|Hughes]]}}</ref> working on [[microwave]] devices and designing [[integrated circuit]]s using gold and silicon [[Schottky diode|Schottky diodes.]]<ref name="web-bio">{{cite web |title=Biography - Warren P. Waters |url=http://warrenpwaters.org/biography/ |access-date=24 June 2015 |website=warrenpwaters.org}}</ref> His patent (with Belardi) is part of the [[Smithsonian Institution|Smithsonian]] Chip Collection.<ref name="MountingArrays-ICs">{{cite journal |author1=Warren P. Waters |author2=Richard J. Belardi |date=25 May 1967 |title=Electrical Connection And/Or Mounting Arrays For Integrated Circuit Chips |url=http://smithsonianchips.si.edu/patents/3518751.htm |access-date=24 June 2015}}</ref>

In his obituary, the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' reported that Waters' integrated circuit designs were used in [[NASA]]'s [[Surveyor program]], which landed some of the first unmanned spacecraft on the Moon.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=The Los Angeles Times 22 Jul 2000, page Page 246 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/162013240 |access-date=2022-11-14 |website=Newspapers.com |language=en}}</ref> The [[Atomic Heritage Foundation]] credits him with developing the components used in the landing mechanisms; later Waters helped invent the [[Wafer (electronics)|silicon wafer]] used in the electronics for telecommunication satellites.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite patent|number=US3836991A|title=Semiconductor device having epitaxial region of predetermined thickness|gdate=1974-09-17|invent1=Portnoy|invent2=Waters|invent3=Wisman|inventor1-first=W.|inventor2-first=W.|inventor3-first=E.|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US3836991/en}}</ref>

In 1980, Waters joined [[Rockwell International]] to work on silicon wafer [[Doping (semiconductor)|doping]]. In 1987, he worked for [[Western Digital]] on silicon disk purification and the development of early computer [[hard disk drive]]s.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="web-bio" />

== Personal life and death ==
Waters married Lois Lockwood in 1951<ref name=marriage>{{cite news|title=Puente Girl Is Married in Pasadena Church Ceremony|issue=Pg 2|publisher=La Puente Valley Journal|date=23 August 1951}}</ref> in what the ''Covina Argus-Citizen'' called "an impressive ceremony";<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=1951-08-24 |title=Impressive Ceremony Unites Lois Lockwood, Warren Waters |pages=5 |work=Covina Argus-Citizen |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/68462542/marriage-announcement/ |access-date=2022-11-14}}</ref> the wedding was reported in several local newspapers.<ref name="marriage-sanger">{{cite news |date=30 August 1951 |title=Sunset Wedding In Pasadena United Lois Virginia Lockwood and Warren Palmer Waters |publisher=Sanger Herald}}</ref> He was the father of three children: Andrea Rosney, conductor [[Carolyn Waters Broe]], and Lisa Waters.<ref name=":2" />

Waters died on 17 July 2000 and is buried at [[Pacific View Memorial Park]] in [[Corona del Mar, Newport Beach|Corona del Mar, California]].<ref name=":2" />

== Waters patents ==

* {{US Patent|2817609}} ''Alkali Metal Alloy Agents for Auto-Fluxing in Junction Forming'', filed June 24, 1955, issued Dec. 24, 1957
* {{US Patent|2829992}} ''Fused Junction Semiconductor Devices and Method of Making Same'', filed Feb. 2, 1954, issued April 8, 1958
* {{US Patent|2829993}} ''Process for Making Fused Junction Semiconductor Devices with Alkali Metal-Galium'', filed June 24, 1955, issued April 8, 1958
* {{US Patent|2854366}} ''Method of Making Fused Junction Semiconductor Devices'', filed Nov. 25, 1957, issued Sept. 30, 1958
* {{US Patent|2854610}} ''Semiconductor Transistor Device'', filed Mar. 24, 1955, issued Sept. 30, 1958
* {{US Patent|3088856}} ''Fused Junction Semiconductor Devices,'' filed Sept. 2, 1955, issued May 7, 1963
* {{US Patent|3388000}} ''Method of Forming a Metal Contact on a Semi Conductor Device'', filed Sept. 18, 1964, issued June 11, 1968
* {{US Patent|3518751}} ''Electrical Connection and/or Mounting Arrays for Integrated Circuit Chips'', filed May 25, 1967, issued July 7, 1970<ref name="MountingArrays-ICs" />
* {{US Patent|3615929}} ''Method of Forming Epitaxial Region of Predetermined Thickness and Article of Manufacture'', filed July 8, 1965, issued Oct. 26, 1971
* {{US Patent|3651384}} ''Planar Schottky Barrier'', filed March 8, 1971, issued Mar. 21, 1972
* {{US Patent|3836991}} ''Semiconductor Device Having Epitaxial Region of Predetermined Thickness'', filed Feb. 23, 1973, issued Sept. 17, 1974
